title: One Security Deposit Account per Lease
content:
**Clause.** One Security Deposit Account secures one lease, and a resident holds one open lease. A deposit account may be opened only when the lease has no other deposit account. An in-community transfer keeps the same deposit account. Pet deposits are added to the same account rather than held in a separate one.

**Basis of the test.** Whether the lease already has a deposit account is read from the company's system records for that lease, not from what the applicant says. Every existing deposit account of the lease counts, whatever its status: pending funding, held, move-out review, statement issued, in collections, or closed.

| Situation in the records | May a new deposit account be opened for this lease? |
|---|---|
| The lease has no deposit account | Yes |
| The lease already has a deposit account, whatever its status | No |

**Limit.** At most 1 deposit account per lease, and a resident holds 1 open lease.

**Related points.**

- *Moving to another apartment home in the same community.* The existing deposit account stays in place for the new apartment home. No new account is opened.
- *Adding a pet.* An additional pet deposit is received into the lease's existing account. No second account is opened for it.
- *A lease whose earlier account is closed.* That account is still a deposit account of the lease, so no new one is opened for the same lease.
